item.title: [Due in 7 days] Teams user reporting switches on by default unless you opt out before 25 October
item.description:
A reporting channel that turns itself on changes what reaches the submissions queue and what the mailbox owners see, and the settings move to a new Defender portal page on 7 October before the default lands on 25 October.

Defender XDR · deadline 2026-10-25 · Open the Teams user-reported settings page in the Defender portal, decide whether reported Teams content goes to Microsoft, and set it before 25 October 2026. Existing email user-reported settings carry over; changes made after the migration may not show until the week of 15 October.

item.title: [New] Sentinel permissions in Defender Unified RBAC can now be assigned to GDAP user groups; service principals still cannot
item.description:
A partner's GDAP group can now hold Sentinel permissions through Unified RBAC, which widens who outside the tenant can read or change Sentinel data once Sentinel is activated in Unified RBAC.

Sentinel · Review GDAP relationships and their groups before activating Sentinel in Unified RBAC; keep automation service principals on Azure RBAC.

item.title: [New] Vulnerability assessment for Microsoft Store applications is generally available in Defender Vulnerability Management
item.description:
Store-installed Teams, Firefox, Slack or WhatsApp were a blind spot in software inventory; GA means their CVEs now count in exposure score and recommendations, so numbers may rise without any new install.

MDE · Expect exposure-score movement on devices with Store apps; check the software inventory for Store-installed browsers and messengers and decide whether they are allowed.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] EmailPostDeliveryEvents gains an ApproverUpn column naming who approved a post-delivery remediation
item.description:
Who approved a soft-delete or move of delivered mail was only in the Action center; having it in hunting lets you audit manual remediation and catch an approval made by an account that should not be approving.

Defender XDR · Add ApproverUpn to any post-delivery remediation report and run the hunting query in this brief to list approvals by approver; use column_ifexists until the column reaches your tenant.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Defender Antivirus platform 4.18.26090.9 and engine 1.1.26090.9 fix dropped ASR exclusions and a sensor left switched off
item.description:
Devices on the older platform may have run with ASR exclusions missing or the behaviour-monitoring network sensor off without anyone choosing that; scripts reading ControlledConfigurationState break on the new platform.

MDE · Report devices below platform 4.18.26090.9, check DisableBmNetworkSensor on them, and update compliance scripts to read ConfigurationProtection.

item.title: [New] Defender for Cloud replaces the Resource Graph query that finds SQL servers protected through Azure Monitor Agent
item.description:
A saved copy of the old query can undercount SQL servers that are actually covered, which skews a coverage report used to decide where to deploy.

Azure · Replace saved copies of the query in workbooks and reports with the new one before the next coverage review.

item.title: [New] Defender XDR multitenant Unified RBAC: creating, deleting and importing custom roles across tenants is no longer preview
item.description:
One change in the managing tenant now lands in every managed tenant by design, so the people who can create or import roles there hold the keys to every customer's Defender permissions.

Defender XDR · List who in the managing tenant can create, edit and import multitenant roles, and require review of every role import.

item.title: [New] Defender real-time protection for AI agents names four threat scenarios it can block: malicious content, secret exfiltration, evasion and unsafe email domains
item.description:
It tells the SOC which agent-abuse cases a blocking rule actually covers; prompt injection that does not fall into one of the four is not claimed.

Defender XDR · Turn on blocking for secret exfiltration and unsafe email domain first, and keep detection-only for the others until you have reviewed a week of alerts.

item.title: [Learn] Defender for Office 365: Expanding user reporting in Teams to include meetings
item.description:
Users can report scheduled or Meet now Microsoft Teams meetings or individual meeting participants as a security concern during or after the meeting. Users can also report a meeting participant that was incorrectly identified as suspicious as not a security concern. Depending on Teams user reported settings, reported meeting and participant metadata is sent to the specified reporting mailbox, to Microsoft, or both.

item.title: [New] Security Operator is now documented as able to disable, enable, revoke sessions and force a password change on Entra ID accounts from Defender for Identity
item.description:
Security Operator is a common SOC analyst role. If the page reflects the service, holders of it can now disable an Entra ID account, revoke its sessions or force its password change from the identity page in Defender XDR, which is a containment power and also a way to lock out an administrator.

MDI · List Security Operator assignments (including PIM-eligible) and confirm each holder should be able to disable accounts and force password changes; alert on these remediation actions in the Defender XDR action center and the Entra audit log when performed by a Security Operator.

item.title: [New] Device tags: the DeviceTagging registry value carries only one tag, and tags set elsewhere are never written back to it
item.description:
Device groups, RBAC scoping and automation often key on tags; a script that reads the registry to decide a device's tags, or that writes several tags there, gets the wrong answer.

MDE · Check scripts and detections that read HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Advanced Threat Protection\DeviceTagging Group for tag membership and read the full set from DeviceInfo in advanced hunting instead, where DeviceManualTags, DeviceDynamicTags and RegistryDeviceTag are separate columns.

item.title: [New] File Integrity Monitoring in Defender for Servers: enabling or changing it now needs Owner and Security Admin on the subscription that holds the Log Analytics workspace
item.description:
File Integrity Monitoring is a detection control: whoever can change its rules can stop the monitoring of a registry key or a system path before tampering with it. The page now places that right at subscription Owner plus Security Admin rather than a workspace-level owner, and it now names changing the configuration, not only switching it on and off.

Azure · List who holds Owner and Security Admin on the subscription that contains the FIM Log Analytics workspace and confirm each is expected; alert on Defender for Servers settings writes (Microsoft.Security/pricings) in the Azure Activity log for that subscription; give SOC analysts who only read FIM results the Security Reader role.
